To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

radiological reports of lumbar spine X- rays for primary care referred patients contain many words describing normal appearances and age-related changes, and very few words indicating that such changes are normal for age.
radiologists use a variety of words to describe the appearance of lumbar spine X- rays and the majority of these words indicate degenerative changes.

the majority of words used by radiographers to describe lumbar X-rays are descriptive and do not indicate the presence of pathology, and that the words used to indicate the presence of pathological conditions are frequently used to indicate normal appearances or age-related changes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the words used by general practitioner-requested X-ray reports to describe lumbar X-rays.
the way in which X-rays are described by radiologists.
how patients are informed about the results of their X-ray.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
74% of reports contained words that indicated that the X-ray was normal.
33% of the reports contained no words indicating the presence or absence of pathology.
the X-ray reports of lumbar spine X rays contain words that are likely to influence patient understanding of the X-ray findings and may therefore influence patient outcome.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the majority of words used by radiographers in X-ray reports of patients with back pain are either descriptive of the anatomy or descriptive of the presence of age-related changes.
radiologists use words that indicate the presence of degeneration in a high proportion of X-ray reports, but do not indicate that these changes are normal for a given age.
X-ray reports are dominated by descriptions of age-related changes.
The main takeaway from our work is that

radiologists tend to describe X-ray findings in terms of age-related changes and other features, which may lead patients and their GPs to believe that their pain is caused by these changes and that their pain is therefore normal for their age.
the majority of the words describing lumbar spine X- rays were descriptive rather than diagnostic.
the words used to describe the lumbar spine in X-ray reports are not neutral, but rather are often used to describe age-related changes.
